mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods following low FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 5.5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) alongside rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, which is positive for S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods with strong PAYEMS and rising UNRATE, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) during an expansion regime signals strong economic fundamentals, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods during expansion with GDP growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods with rising INDPRO, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in real consumer spending (RSAFS) below 2% growth signals weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the periods with RSAFS growth below 2%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) alongside increasing FEDFUNDS indicates tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in 60% of the periods with rising CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% in a late expansion phase signals a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in 60% of the periods with UNRATE below 4.5% during late expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.
